{"id":"mimid-f9x4.1","title":"The keepalive draft's jitter and its 3x floor can disagree","description":"Implementing the keepalive on the live stream (bead mimid-mm42) found one
place where 4.1 and 4.3 of the draft can both be satisfied only by luck,
and one sentence of 4.3 that no binding can obey as written.

ONE. 4.3 lets the prober choose any P with minIntervalSeconds <= P, and
requires each interval to be P randomized between 0.8 and 1.2. At P =
minIntervalSeconds, two intervals in ten fall below minIntervalSeconds,
which the same section lets the responder answer tooFrequent and which the
prober must then wait out. A prober that wants every interval at or above
minIntervalSeconds needs P >= 1.25 x minIntervalSeconds, so it needs
3.75 x minIntervalSeconds < maxIdleSeconds, not the 3 x of 4.1. A responder
that states exactly 3 x minIntervalSeconds + 1 therefore offers a range in
which no jitter-safe P exists, while satisfying 4.1.

Three ways out, none chosen here:

  - raise the floor in 4.1 from 3 to 3.75 (or 4), so that a legal pair
    always admits a jitter-safe P;
  - say in 4.3 that the jitter is applied upward only, 1.0 to 1.4 of P,
    which keeps every interval at or above minIntervalSeconds and keeps
    desynchronization;
  - say in 4.3 that an interval shorter than minIntervalSeconds is the
    prober's own affair and that a responder MUST NOT answer tooFrequent
    to a probe inside the jitter window, which is hard to state without
    naming the window.

The live stream dodges it: the prober picks the largest legal P rather than
the smallest, its carrier's probe is a WebSocket Ping, and nothing answers
a Ping tooFrequent. A binding whose probe is the draft's own
KeepAliveRequest cannot dodge it.

TWO. 4.3 requires a responder that changes either value to "answer one
further probe paced by the previous values". A responder that restates its
values in a KeepAliveResponse (4.1 requires it in every response) cannot
tell whether the probe it is now answering was paced by the old values or
the new ones: nothing in the request says which values the prober held, and
the nonce names nothing. The requirement is satisfiable only as a timer --
do not refuse or reap for one previous-maxIdleSeconds after the change --
which is what the second half of the same paragraph already says. The first
half can go.

NEITHER IS IMPLEMENTED HERE. The live stream states one pair per carrier
and never changes it, so TWO costs mimid nothing today; ONE is avoided by
the choice of P recorded in decision mimid-1wgh.137. Both belong in the
draft before it is sent, which is why this bead exists rather than a code
change.
","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-28T04:59:24.443630528Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-28T04:59:24.443630528Z","labels":["human","wg"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"mimid-f9x4.1","depends_on_id":"mimid-f9x4","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-11-28T04:59:24.4873302Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}
new_value: {"notes":"ALSO, from the same implementation: §4.5's revalidation asks nothing of a binding whose prober probes continuously. An end that probes on the pair it was told has either heard from the other inside the idle tolerance or declared the carrier dead, so delivery traffic only ever goes on a carrier that answered inside it. §4.5 earns its place only where a prober stops probing an idle carrier, which the draft never says it may do; saying that it may, and then requiring revalidation, would make the section bite."}

new_value: The code half is done, in commit 698c0c57 (worktree branch worktree-agent-a9889aaccba9e6556): crates/mimid-live enforces and obeys the corrected floor. Keepalive::new refuses a pair unless 15 x minIntervalSeconds is under 4 x maxIdleSeconds, in u128 so the comparison is exact for every pair of u64s the wire can carry; PACING_FLOOR_NUMERATOR and PACING_FLOOR_DENOMINATOR hold the ratio, derived from PROBES_PER_IDLE and JITTER_LOW_PERMILLE. Keepalive::period returns the largest legal base period in whole milliseconds, which satisfies both of the prober's conditions (4 x P at least 5 x minIntervalSeconds, 3 x P under maxIdleSeconds) for every pair new accepts; whole seconds would not, since 1 and 6 admits no legal whole second. 30 and 120 stay the offered pair, 450 under 480, and a test asserts the rule of the offered pair rather than the numbers. Tests moved to the new boundary (30 and 91, 2 and 7, 4 and 15 refused; 30 and 113, 2 and 8, 4 and 16 accepted) and a sweep of every pair up to 64 by 1024 asserts the rule and the two period conditions agree. docs/design/binary-live-stream.md CDDL and 5.12 carry the new rule, the derivation and the millisecond period. The draft half was already corrected by Mark earlier today (commits 8325ec89 and 0274fde2); nothing of the draft was written here. Fixture bytes are unchanged, 30 and 120 being legal either way, with the comment lines and PROVENANCE SHA-256s updated.
